chunks: 35. My father (ra) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (AS) who said:

I heard him say: Whoever says in a day: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the One and Only, who has no partners; the God [ilah], the One [wahid], the Unique [ahad], on whom all depend, who has not taken a partner nor son,' Allah, the Majestic and Glorious, will record for him 45 thousand thousand good deeds, and erase from him 45 thousand thousand evil deeds, and raise for him in Paradise 45 thousand thousand degrees, and he will be like one who recited the Quran twelve times, and Allah will build a house for him in Paradise.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting the specific declaration of monotheism mentioned in al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith highlights the eschatological weight of *Tawhid al-Ikhlas* (pure monotheism) within Shia devotional practice, linking verbal affirmation to tangible spiritual accounting. The specific metric of 45 million rewards underscores the concept of *Ihya al-Quran* (reviving the Quran) through concise, potent declarations, a theme central to the school of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the efficacy of dhikr.
